ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Patient awoke ~1 hour prior unable to move left arm; no precipitating event or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Symptoms began on waking, persisted throughout call; no improvement.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Dysphagia – patient “having a bit of issues” swallowing drinks.  
  • Speech difficulty – slower, harder to articulate.  
  • Tingling/numbness left side of face.  
  • Denies facial asymmetry noted visually.  
  • No throat tightness, voice change/hoarseness, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, or oral/facial swelling reported.  
  • No ear pain/hearing change, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No prior similar episodes; no prior hospitalizations for these symptoms.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Current medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Losartan (dose/route/frequency not documented); Amlodipine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Relevant social context: Lives alone; no one present at home during episode.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor or respiratory distress reported; voice subjectively slower but audible.
- Mental status: Alert, oriented; able to answer questions; speech slowed.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telephone consultation).
- Presence of another person: None.

Assessment:
- Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (stroke) with associated dysphagia and speech changes; ENT relevance primarily airway protection/aspiration risk in setting of neurologic deficit.

Plan:
- Emergency action: GP service arranged immediate ambulance dispatch to patient’s home.
- Safety instructions: Patient advised to unlock front door, sit in hallway to enable EMS access; clinician remained on the telephone line until EMS arrival.
- Escalation criteria/red flags reviewed implicitly by arranging EMS (worsening speech, inability to protect airway, progression of neurologic deficit).
- Follow-up: Management to continue in emergency department with stroke team; no outpatient ENT follow-up arranged at this stage.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: On-scene vitals, direct airway/cranial nerve examination, swallow assessment, availability of caregiver, blood glucose reading, ENT physical exam findings.
● Internal conflicts: None identified in transcript.
● Transcript quality: Clear two-way telephone conversation; no significant audio gaps, though objective physical findings limited by remote format.
